messages.author: a8ba3a2201b6ba7d
messages.subject: 2^31-1 byte limit
parts:
Hi,

My dataset has 40,937,390 data points, each representing bird migratory stopover density in a 1km x 1km cell in a year. I am fitting an spde model of migratory stopover and I get the error:

 *** inla.core.safe:  The inla program failed, but will rerun in case better initial values may help. try=1/1
Warning in iinla(model = info[["model"]], lhoods = info[["lhoods"]], options = info[["options"]]) :
  iinla: Problem in inla: Error in paste0(vapply(x, function(x) { :
  result would exceed 2^31-1 bytes
iinla: Problem in inla:
iinla: Giving up and returning last successfully obtained result for diagnostic purposes.

When I aggregate the data to 4km x 4km cells, it fits fine.

I think the the 2^31-1 byte limit is imposed by R on character vectors, in which case increasing the memory and processing power of the computer wouldn't help.

Is there anything about the mesh or the model components that I could change to reduce the size of the character vector that inla has to save while fitting the model?

Thanks in advance for any help!

My mesh is made as folllows (units are km):
mesh =fm_mesh_2d_inla(boundary = list(radar_buffer_80_ag), max.edge = c(25, 500), offset = 500, crs = fm_crs(data))

And this these are the model components and formula:
# components
svc_components <- ~ -1 +
  alpha(cell, model = "iid", hyper = list(prec = pc_prec), constr = TRUE) +
  kappa(geometry, model = spde)

# formula
svc_formula <- stopover ~ .

#fit
res_1 <- bru(
  svc_components,
    like(formula = svc_formula,
    family = "gamma",
    data = data
    ),
  options = list(
    control.compute = list(waic = TRUE, cpo = FALSE),
    control.inla = list(
      int.strategy = "eb"
    ),
    verbose = TRUE,
    bru_verbose = 4
  )
)

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] 2^31-1 byte limit
parts:
Hi,

I think the 2^31 message may be due to a bug in the error reporting code and that the actual error is something else. The error reporting code has been updated in the development versions, so try installing fmesher and inlabru from github or the inlabru r-universe repository. Then run your code again to hopefully get a different error message.

I'm on holiday this week, so if the real problem is in inlabru itself I can't help more until next week.

Finn
